clue.text: Violent floods disrupting calm is when unsuspecting victims are caught out

definitions.text: when unsuspecting victims are caught out

indicators.note: disrupting says the scrambled letters break into the middle of the word for calm

parts.note: to allay is to calm or soothe

indicators.note: violent upheaval throws the letters of floods into a new order

explanation.surface: Raging floodwaters shattering the peace of a quiet place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Violent' looks like a description of the floods, but it signals the anagram; 'calm' is a verb here, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: April 1st is the traditional date for pranks, when gullible people are tricked and mocked.

clue.text: Lively member joining in a student run out

indicators.note: joining in says the limb enters the middle of the other letters

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate, standing for a student
RO is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out
a leg is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: An energetic new club member joins a student who has been run out at cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman 'run out' is scored RO.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegro is the musical direction for a brisk, lively tempo.

clue.text: Baffled US agent leaving for 23

indicators.note: leaving says the agent's letters go out of the longer word

parts.note: flummoxed means baffled or bewildered
a fed is an American slang term for an FBI agent

explanation.surface: A bewildered American agent quits, standing in for a colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 is FOOL, the second word of 12/23; 'for' just links. FED departs from F-LUMMOX-ED in two scattered pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A lummox is a clumsy, stupid person, a synonym for a fool.

clue.text: Where palms may be found in every direction

definitions.meaning: a palm is the inside of a hand
an idiom meaning on every side, everywhere

explanation.surface: Where palm trees grow on every side.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally every hand has a palm; idiomatically the phrase means all around, from every quarter.

clue.text: Split appearing among upwardly mobile Microsoft Fellows

indicators.note: upwardly mobile says the hidden letters are read backwards
appearing among says the answer sits inside the run of the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Ambitious senior staff at Microsoft fall out with each other.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Split appearing among' as the definition, but 'appearing among' is the hidden-word signal, so the definition is just 'Split'. TFEL spans microsofT FELlows; read upwards in this down clue it gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To split is informal for to leave or depart, and the past tense matches the answer.

clue.text: Deviated from route winding through heart of Puy-de-Dome

indicators.note: through says the twisted letters pass inside the central letters
heart of picks the central letters of the French place name
a winding path twists the letters of route into another order

explanation.surface: A traveller strayed off course on a winding road in the Auvergne's volcanic heart.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of PUYDEDOME is DED; 'winding' makes TOURE from ROUTE, set 'through' it.
explanation.definitionFit: To detour is to take a roundabout way, so a traveller who detoured deviated from the direct path.

clue.text: Flourished with unknown as stopgap leader, then surrendered

indicators.note: a stopgap stands in temporarily, so the unknown takes the place of the first letter

parts.note: to flourish a sword is to wield it
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: Someone thrived under a caretaker boss, then gave up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flourished' is the brandishing sense, not thriving. Y replaces the first W.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield is to give way or give up, so yielded is a synonym for surrendered.

clue.text: Hat back-to-front, girl in predicament

indicators.note: back-to-front says the word for hat is written in reverse

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat
Emma is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl wearing her hat the wrong way round is in a fix.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilemma is a difficult choice, a tricky situation or predicament.

clue.text: Deals grass shiftily — kilo wrapped as shown in Polaroids?

indicators.note: wrapped says the scrambled letters go around the abbreviation
acting shiftily, the letters of deals grass are moved about

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for kilo, and Kilo is K in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A shady dealer sells marijuana, a kilo hidden, as photographed in instant pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polaroids' suggests instant photos but here means sunglasses with polarising lenses; 'as shown in' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: Polaroid is a brand of polarised sunglasses, so Polaroids are an example of tinted spectacles.

clue.text: Dad's resistance is spent, getting notice for 23

indicators.note: spent means used up and gone, so the letter disappears

parts.note: dad is father
R is the symbol for electrical resistance
an ad is a notice or advertisement

explanation.surface: Dad has given up resisting and gets a warning for being foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 is FOOL, from 12/23.
explanation.definitionFit: A fathead is a stupid person, a colloquial synonym for a fool.

clue.text: Mother mounting missing diamonds in decoration

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother

indicators.note: missing says the suit letter is lost from the climbing word

parts.note: mounting means ascending, climbing
D is the abbreviation for diamonds, the card suit

explanation.surface: A mother setting stones notices the diamonds have gone from an ornament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mounting' looks like setting gems but means climbing.
explanation.definitionFit: Damascening is inlaying gold or silver patterns into steel, an ornamental metalwork technique.

clue.text: Cuddly toys gad about in posh car

indicators.note: in says the scrambled letters sit inside the car

parts.note: a Rolls is a Rolls-Royce, the classic posh car

indicators.note: about signals the letters of gad are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: Soft toys gallivanting around in a luxury limousine.
explanation.walkthrough: A Rolls is a Rolls-Royce; 'gad about' reads as one phrase, but 'about' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Rag dolls are soft dolls made of cloth, the kind of toy a child cuddles.

clue.text: 23's bullet?

definitions.meaning: 23 is fool; slang for a stupid person, a fool
a soft-nosed bullet that expands on impact

explanation.surface: A fool's ammunition?
explanation.walkthrough: 23 is FOOL, from 12/23.
explanation.definitionFit: Dumdum is both slang for a dimwit and the name of an expanding bullet, first made at Dum Dum in India.

clue.text: Sweet Nellie, pursuing undesirable member of group

indicators.note: pursuing says this word comes after the other

parts.note: to play gooseberry is to be the unwanted third person with a couple
a nellie (or nelly) is British slang for a silly person, a fool

explanation.surface: Sweet Nellie trailing behind an unwanted companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' looks like an adjective for Nellie but is the definition. A gooseberry is the British term for an unwanted third party on a date.
explanation.definitionFit: Gooseberry fool is a British dessert, a sweet of fruit purée folded into cream.

clue.text: Sticky stuff's fine for 23

parts.note: goo is sticky, gooey material
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads

explanation.surface: Some glue serves as a substitute for something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 is FOOL, from 12/23.
explanation.definitionFit: A goof is an informal word for a silly or foolish person.

clue.text: Friend ended some Gallic 'prickly affairs'

definitions.note: plural answer for plural affairs; the trees are the spiny things

parts.note: a pal is a friend
over means finished, ended
des is French for some

explanation.surface: A friend broke off some French romances that had become thorny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affairs' is informal for things, here spiny desert trees; the quotation marks flag the playful sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Palo verde is a thorny desert tree of the American Southwest, so a group of them are spiny plants.

clue.text: Wrongly under a cloud, due painfully to depart in large vessel

indicators.note: wrongly says the letters of under a cloud are rearranged
painfully says the letters of due leave in any order, so they are taken out of the pool

explanation.surface: Someone wrongly suspected, with a bill painfully due, leaves aboard a big ship.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: remove D, U, E from the letters of UNDER A CLOUD and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A cauldron is a large metal pot, a vessel for boiling.

clue.text: Rig agendas cunningly and increase power

indicators.note: doing something cunningly suggests manipulation, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A schemer fixes meeting agendas to gain more influence.
explanation.definitionFit: To aggrandise is to enhance the power, status or wealth of someone.

clue.text: Accident on the ropes, say, in 'Pinafore'?

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed after

parts.note: climbing ropes are found in a gym, so the ropes exemplify a gym
a slip is a minor accident or mistake

explanation.surface: A mishap on the stage rigging during a performance of Gilbert and Sullivan's HMS Pinafore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pinafore' hints at the operetta but means the dress. A gymslip is the sleeveless tunic once worn by British schoolgirls.
explanation.definitionFit: A gymslip is a sleeveless pinafore dress worn over a blouse as school uniform.

clue.text: Protestant grouping acquires base in 23

indicators.note: acquires says the base letter is added to the party

parts.note: the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland, a Protestant-rooted party
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: A political party gains a foothold among fools.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 is FOOL, from 12/23. The DUP is a unionist party in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A dupe is someone easily deceived, a gullible fool.

clue.text: We hear you managed one interjection — that's elemental!

definitions.note: an exclamation standing for a noun: the answer is a chemical element

indicators.note: we hear says the words are spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: you ran, meaning you managed, run a business
I is the Roman numeral one
um is a hesitant interjection

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that a simple trick is elementary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you ran' said aloud gives URAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Uranium is a radioactive chemical element, so it is literally elemental.

clue.text: 23's nervous carrying weight on the climb

indicators.note: climbing upward in a down clue means the letters read from bottom to top
carrying says the shy word holds the weight letter

parts.note: timid means nervous or shy

explanation.surface: A fool is anxious while carrying a load up a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 is FOOL, from 12/23. 'carrying' gives TIWMID, which 'on the climb' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: A dimwit is a stupid person, a synonym for a fool.

clue.text: Swatch of satin initially rather bulky

indicators.note: initially says take the opening letter of satin

parts.note: ample means large or rather bulky

explanation.surface: A fabric swatch of satin that is a bit chunky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swatch' looks like part of the fabric scene but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A swatch is a small piece of fabric shown as a sample.

clue.text: With balti, I go bananas creating essential accompaniments

indicators.note: going bananas is going crazy, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A curry eater goes wild for the side dishes that must come with a balti.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go bananas' reads as one phrase, but GO is fodder with BALTI and I; 'bananas' alone signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Obbligati are musical parts that must not be omitted, essential accompanying lines.

clue.text: See 12
Port of New Orleans

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh arrangement of the letters of Orleans

explanation.surface: A port belonging to the Louisiana city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Orleans' reads as one name, but 'New' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Salerno is a seaport in southern Italy.

clue.text: Author arguing about ending of novel

indicators.note: about says the quarrelling word goes round that letter

parts.note: rowing (rhymes with cowing) is British for quarrelling

indicators.note: ending of picks the last letter of novel

explanation.surface: A writer quarrels over how a book should end.
explanation.walkthrough: ROWING here means quarrelling, rhyming with 'cow', not boating.
explanation.definitionFit: J. K. Rowling is the author of the Harry Potter books.

clue.text: Arrangements for imprisonment confine a large, sadly deserted family

parts.note: to pen is to shut in, confine

indicators.note: deserted means emptied, leaving only the outside letters of sadly

parts.note: stem means a line of descent, a family

explanation.surface: Locking up a big family who have sadly been abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deserted' empties SADLY to SY.
explanation.definitionFit: A penal system is the organised set of prisons and punishments a state uses.
